extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates and graduate students in mathematics (asymptotic analysis, analytic number theory)
extracted.subtask_short: asymptotic analysis of integrals and sequences
extracted.subtask_description: Techniques and conditions for deriving asymptotic expansions of integrals, special functions, and sequence coefficients (e.g., partition function) via contour deformation, Laplace's method, stationary phase, steepest descent, and generating-function analysis. Includes precise hypotheses and error estimates for standard propositions and theorems (Stirling, Bessel, Airy, Hardy–Ramanujan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle: deformation of contour
rubrics_metrics.description: When Φ is holomorphic, change the contour of integration so that on the new contour Φ is essentially real-valued; this reduces oscillation and reveals the dominant contribution to I(s)=∫_a^b e^{-sΦ(x)} dx for large s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use analytic continuation / Cauchy theorem to move contour to regions where the integrand decays (exponential factor becomes real-decaying). Illustrated in Bessel and Airy examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle: Laplace's method (endpoint and interior minima)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Φ is real-valued on the contour and s>0, the main contribution to ∫ e^{-sΦ} comes from minima of Φ; expansions follow from quadratic behavior near the minimum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the minimum occurs at an endpoint, use Proposition 1.2; if in the interior and Φ''(x0)>0 use Proposition 2.1 to obtain leading order ~ e^{-sΦ(x0)}·A·s^{-1/2} with A = sqrt(2π) ψ(x0)/√{Φ''(x0)}. Error estimates: O(1/s) or exponentially small remainders from other regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle: generating-functions method
rubrics_metrics.description: Asymptotic behavior of a sequence {F_n} can be obtained from analytic properties of its generating function F(w)=∑ F_n w^n; use contour integral representations F_n = ∮ F(e^{2π i z}) e^{-2π i n z} dz and analyze via integral-asymptotic methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heuristic: dominant singularities of F on the unit circle determine the asymptotic of F_n; the 'order' / nature of each singularity controls the magnitude of its contribution. Applied to partition function p(n).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 1.2: endpoint Laplace integral (real s)
rubrics_metrics.description: For fixed a>0 and m>-1, as s→∞, ∫_0^a e^{-s x} x^m dx = s^{-m-1} Γ(m+1) + O(e^{-c s}) for some c>0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via splitting integral at a and change of variables x→x/s; remainder estimated by exponential decay. Use when main contribution is from x near 0 (endpoint).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 1.3: endpoint Laplace integral (complex s)
rubrics_metrics.description: For fixed a>0 and -1<m<0, as |s|→∞ with Re(s)≥0, ∫_0^a e^{-s x} x^m dx = s^{-m-1} Γ(m+1) + O(1/|s|).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extends Proposition 1.2 to complex s with Re(s)≥0 (principal branch for s^{-m-1}). Use integration by parts and analytic continuation; error O(1/|s|) arises from endpoint contribution when m<0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 1.1: Bessel Jν asymptotic
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived by expressing J_ν as integral I(s) = ∫_{-1}^1 e^{i s x} (1-x^2)^{ν-1/2} dx and deforming contour to lines near x=±1 where exponential decays (I_+, I_-). Use Proposition 1.2 for the endpoint contributions; include Gamma factors in prefactor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 2.1: Laplace method for interior nondegenerate minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: If Φ,ψ are smooth on [a,b], Φ attains a unique minimum at x0∈(a,b) with Φ(x0)=0 and Φ''(x0)>0, then as s→∞ (s>0), ∫_a^b e^{-sΦ(x)} ψ(x) dx = e^{-sΦ(x0)}·A·s^{-1/2} + O(1/s), where A = √(2π) ψ(x0)/√{Φ''(x0)}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change variables to reduce to Gaussian integral; remainder terms from outside small neighborhood decay exponentially or are O(1/s). Useful when stationary point is interior and nondegenerate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 2.2: complex-s extension of Laplace interior-minimum asymptotic
rubrics_metrics.description: Same asymptotic as Proposition 2.1 continues to hold as |s|→∞ with Re(s)≥0 (complex s), provided Φ,ψ smooth and critical point nondegenerate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle oscillatory behavior for large imaginary part by integration by parts; show uniform estimates on complementary intervals where |Φ'|≥c>0 to obtain O(1/|s|) bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 2.3: Stirling's formula (sectorial form)
rubrics_metrics.description: If |s|→∞ with s in sector S_δ = {s: |arg s| ≤ π-δ}, then Γ(s) = e^{s log s - s} √(2π) s^{-1/2} (1 + O(1/|s|^{1/2})).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce Γ(s) to an integral of Laplace type via x→s x; apply Proposition 2.2 at x0=1 where Φ(x)=x-1-log x has Φ(1)=Φ'(1)=0 and Φ''(1)=1. Estimate tails by integration by parts; extend to full sector using functional relations Γ(s)Γ(-s)=π/(-s sin πs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of stationary phase
rubrics_metrics.description: For integrals with purely imaginary large parameter (s = it, t→±∞) and real phase Φ, main contributions come from stationary points where Φ'(x)=0; asymptotics involve oscillatory terms with amplitude ~ t^{-1/2} determined by Φ'' at the stationary points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Proposition 2.2 specialized to purely imaginary s. Example: Airy function Ai(-u) yields oscillatory asymptotics by splitting integral around critical points ±1 of Φ(x)=x^3/3 - x.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of steepest descent (choice of contour)
rubrics_metrics.description: To analyze integrals ∫ e^{-s F(z)} dz with holomorphic F, choose a contour Γ such that (a) Im(F)=0 on Γ and (b) Re(F) has a nondegenerate minimum at some z0∈Γ; then apply Laplace's method along Γ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At a nonreal critical point z0, the two orthogonal curves where Im(F)=0 give one curve where Re(F) has a minimum (steepest descent) and one where it has a maximum (reject). Example: for Airy integrals, choose Γ through z0=i with equation y^2 = x^2/3 + 1; reduce to real Laplace integral on Γ and apply Proposition 2.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 3.1: Airy function asymptotics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain (i) via stationary phase at real critical points ±1 of Φ(x)=x^3/3 - x; obtain (ii) by deforming contour to steepest-descent path through nonreal critical point and applying Laplace's method. Provide error orders O(1/|t|) or O(u^{-3/4}) as indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heuristic for sequence asymptotics from generating function singularities
rubrics_metrics.description: If F(w)=∑ F_n w^n has unit disc of convergence, the asymptotic behavior of F_n is determined by the location and nature of singularities of F on |w|=1; each singularity contributes according to its 'order'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contour integral representation of coefficients and deform contour toward dominant singularities (saddle points / poles / branch points). Applied to partition function p(n) using modular/θ-function structure to obtain Hardy–Ramanujan asymptotics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 4.1: Hardy–Ramanujan asymptotic for partition function
rubrics_metrics.description: As n→∞, p(n) ∼ (1/(4√3 n)) e^{π √(2n/3)}. A more precise assertion gives a refined leading term involving (n - 1/24)^{−1/2} e^{K (n - 1/24)^{1/2}} and an explicit error O(e^{(K/2) n^{1/2}}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive by applying generating-function methods and contour deformation around the dominant singularity of the partition generating function F(q)=∏_{n≥1} (1-q^n)^{-1}; modular properties and transformation of θ/η functions are exploited to obtain full asymptotic expansion (Hardy–Ramanujan / Rademacher methods).
